name: API Sentinel
summary: Local-first API reliability, runtime intelligence and incident investigation: runtime observation, SLO assessment, anomaly detection, incident investigation and deployment correlation over real telemetry. Diagnoses from runtime evidence; it is not an engineering producer.
appropriate_for: runtime observation of API services from ingested telemetry (metrics, traces, health probes)
anomaly detection and incident investigation from runtime evidence
deployment-correlation questions (did release X regress the service?)
consuming api-forge or forge-doctor-api handoff artifacts for independent runtime diagnosis
inappropriate_for: producing API code or contracts — it is an observer/diagnostician, not a producer
static source review of a repository — route to api-forge or forge-doctor-api
platform estate or CI/CD analysis — route to platform-forge
any run without the telemetry/runs its diagnostics require

install.command: python3.11 -m venv <sentinel-venv> && <sentinel-python> -m pip install --upgrade pip && <sentinel-python> -m pip install "api-sentinel-forge>=0.1.0,<0.2.0" && <sentinel-python> -m pip install -e <checkout-the-forge>/adapters/apisentinel

limitations_note: Diagnostics require runtime evidence (telemetry batches, run dumps, SLO windows): the orchestration lane refuses to force a sentinel diagnosis when the caller declares no such inputs. Profile `local` works fully offline; `aws`/`opentelemetry` profiles degrade to honest unavailable states without their collectors.
examples: is checkout-api breaching its SLO this week?
investigate the 5xx spike after the last deploy
